description.narrative: The development objectives of the Mining Infrastructure Investment Support Project (MINIS) for Mongolia are to facilitate investments in infrastructure to support mining and downstream processing activities, regardless of funding source, and to build local capacity to prepare and transact infrastructure projects. There are four components to the project, the first component being support for infrastructure investments. The project will provide financing to prepare regional infrastructure investment plans, conduct feasibility studies to assess technical options and determine economic and financial implications of proposed projects, and address emerging priority issues as a result of the country's nascent enabling environment governing private participation in infrastructure. The second component is the capacity building and knowledge transfer. A long-term approach for building capacity and developing the requisite skills to prepare infrastructure projects and transactions with investors will be necessary to develop local skills. The third component is the strengthening groundwater management. Support will be provided to strengthen the capacity of local authorities to manage groundwater resources in the region. The government has established a framework of 29 water basins for the entire country. For Southern Mongolia, these basins are centered on groundwater, as surface water is of minor importance in the southern part of the country. It is expected that a new institutional structure will be piloted at two locations in Southern Mongolia with jurisdictional responsibilities defined along groundwater boundary basins. Finally, the fourth component is the project management.

To facilitate investments in infrastructure to support mining and downstream processing activities, regardless of funding source, and to build local capacity to prepare and transact infrastructure projects.

title.narrative: At least two key infrastructure assets ready for tender

baseline.value: Technical/financial understanding to prepare transactions lacking.

target.value: Two transactions are ready for tendering.

actual.value: Substantially achieved: Preparation of subprojects for investments/transaction is measured through the completion of feasibility and safeguards studies. Feasibility studies have been completed for three projects: Baganuur mine expansion, Steel Complex and Synthetic Natural Gas (SNG). Safeguards studies for these three subprojects are planned to be completed by the project closing date, making these three subprojects ready for investments/transaction. Furthermore, the Cumulative Impact Assessment (CIA) for Tavan Tolgoi mie supported under MINIS is also planned for completion by the project closing. The feasibility study for the Tavan Tolgoi mine financed under another Bank supported project has been completed. Thus, by the project closing date, the Tavan Tolgoi Mine project will also be ready for investments/transaction.

comment.narrative:
<p>This has been achieved and exceeded was due to: (i) broadening of the training needs as a result of the diverse nature of priority projects proposed for MINIS support, which had not been envisaged at Design; and (ii) the turnaround in staffing of the counterpart teams in the beneficiary agencies.</p>
<p>* In the PAD and Restructuring Papers, the baseline for Component 2.1 Training program and events was defined as n/a, and the Unit of Measure for Original Target was "10 programs", defined as text.</p>

baseline.value: Insufficient resources/capacity to manage groundwater in Southern Mongolia.

comment.narrative: <p>This has been achieved through the development and implementation of groundwater management plans and online monitoring by telemetry data loggers.</p>

actual.value: Ability to manage groundwater strengthened with the River Basin Administrations (RBAs) established and adequately staffed, groundwater monitoring and management plans in place, monitoring wells set up and operational and the monitoring system functional with databeing collected through online telemetry and routine data assessment through data loggers

title.narrative: Good practice and procedures established to prepare projects for public and private financing

baseline.value: Limited understanding of required studies, no guidelines on economic evaluation.

comment.narrative: <p>This outcome has been achieved as evidenced by the ability to successfully procure and manage consultancy services for project preparation and transaction.</p>

actual.value: Good practice and procedures established to prepare projects for public and private financing, including on procurement of consulting services for feasibility studies and safeguards assessments, implementation of public consultations and incorporation of stakeholder's feedback into project design

title.narrative: Consultants provide hands-on training and help administer government-financed projects & PPP concessions

baseline.value: No concessions to administer.

comment.narrative: <p>This has been partially achieved. Consultants have provided hands-on training to help administer government-financed projects. While good practices related to managing PPP transactions were shared with government staff and decision-makers, projects prepared with MINIS support have so far not been selected for PPP financing, and therefor no consultant was required for help in administering PPP concessions.</p>

actual.value: Consultants provided hands-on training and helped administer government-financed projects as well as planning PPP concessions.

baseline.value: Studies for priority projects not available.

comment.narrative: <p>This has been achieved. The Project supported the Ministry of Mining and Heavy Industry (MMHI) in their preparation of the FSs for two subprojects: the Integrated Steel Complex (ISC) and the Synthetic Natural Gas (SNG).</p>

actual.value: Feasibility studies for the Integrated Steel Complex, Synthetic Natural Gas, Baganuur Coal Mine Expansion projects have been completed.

title.narrative: Rapid response to address issues impacting private investment

baseline.value: Technical/financial support to address issues not available.

comment.narrative: <p>This has been achieved ad evidenced by the incorporation of subprojects' economic demand assessment, technology trade-off considerations, groundwater availability, public consultations and stakeholder management in project preparation and documentation.</p>

actual.value: Rapid responses to address issues impacting private investment were raised and resolved for: subprojects' economic demand assessment, technology trade-off considerations, groundwater availability, public consultations and stakeholder management

title.narrative: At least two key infrastructure assets ready for tender

baseline.value: Technical/financial understanding to prepare transactions lacking.

comment.narrative: <p>This has been substantially achieved. Feasibility studies and/or safeguards assessments for the four aforementioned projects have been prepared. Such preparation allows the projects to be ready for financing if they were to be developed with public funds. This is the intention of the Government, which was communicated to the Bank at Project Closing.</p>

actual.value: Feasibility studies and safeguards assessments have been completed for the Integrated Steel Complex, Synthetic Natural Gas (SNG) and Baganuur Coal Mine Expansion, and a Cumulative Impact Assessment for the Tavan Tolgoi Coal Mine Expansion, helping to facilitate investment in these projects.

comment.narrative: <p>This has been achieved. It includes workshops and conferences to promote better understanding among the business community on the potential investment opportunities in mining and infrastructure in Mongolia.</p>

actual.value: 9 conferences/workshops were organized.

title.narrative: Establishment of 3 RBA in Southern Gobi Region

baseline.value: Insufficient resources/capacity to manage groundwater in Southern Mongolia.

target.value: Building capacity for effective groundwater management.

actual.value: Achieved: The River Basin Adminstrations (RBAs) have been established and adequately staffed; they have become fully operational and GW management and monitoring plans are in place. Groundwater monitoring wells in south Gobi are completed and equipped. Moreover, the monitoring system is functioning and data is being collected through online telemetry for some remote locations and periodic downloading from the other installed data loggers.

title.narrative: Good practice and procedures established to prepare projects for public and private financing

baseline.value: Limited understanding of required studies, no guidelines on economic evaluation.

actual.value: Largely achieved: Trainings on preparation of feasibility studies and financial and economic evaluation was delivered to the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Environment and Tourism, Ministry of Industry and Ministry of Mining. The concerned Ministry started to apply best practice on economic evaluation that was shared with them through trainings.

title.narrative: Consultants provide hands-on training and help administer government-financed projects & PPP concessions

baseline.value: No concessions to administer.

target.value: Staff is well trained to administer government-financed projects & PPP concessions

actual.value: Partially achieved: Five training programs were delivered to the Ministry of Finance and other Ministries in the preparation and processing of seven PPP transactions since 2011. However due to staff turnover in the Ministries, additional capacity building efforts are required.

title.narrative: Promotion of appropriate organization structure for groundwater management established

baseline.value: Preliminary organization structure was in place but not revised

target.value: Development of the appropriate organization structure for the management of the GW in three river basins

actual.value: Achieved: Appropriate organization structure for the management of the GW in three river basins, consisting of 3 RBAs and 3 RBCs, in South Gobi was developed.

baseline.value: Studies for priority projects not available.

target.value: Complete feasibility studies for ongoing infrastructure projects.

actual.value: Achieved: The FS studies for the Baganuur coal mine, Steel Complex and Coal to Gas subprojects have been completed.

title.narrative: Rapid response to address issues impacting private investment

baseline.value: Technical/financial support to address issues not available.

target.value: Rapid response to at least five issues.

actual.value: Achieved: Training on preparation of feasibility studies and financial and economic evaluation was provided to the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Environment Green Development and Tourism. Ministry of Industry and Ministry of Mining, regarding the preparation of feasibility studies and financial and economic evaluation. A number of issues concerning need assessment, information gathering, viability of economic analysis, proper preparation and public consultations were addressed in the course of identifying priority subprojects and the development of the feasibility studies and ESIAs and CIAs.

actual.value: 9 conferences/workshops were attended.
